The parts of a McKinley Park quote that actually move

A 1930 median build year means plaster as well as drywall, and the two do not take a repair the same way. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so the honest version of a wall repair here is longer than a drywall patch and should read that way on the quote. With 5.9 rooms on the median unit, the trim is the other half of the job. With 56.3 percent of units here in buildings of two or more, a lot of the work is unit turnover and common areas rather than whole houses. That is priced per unit and scheduled around a move-out date, not around weather.

Is there lead paint in my house?

The honest answer for a 1930s-era house in McKinley Park is probably yes, there is older paint under there, and paint that old can contain lead. What follows from that is method, not a refusal: sheeting, sealed doorways, dust kept where it is made, and a cleanup McKinley Park homeowners should expect to see done properly.

What it changes is the front and the back of a McKinley Park job, not the middle: plastic and sealed openings before, a specific cleanup standard after. It starts at roughly six square feet of disturbed paint per room inside, twenty square feet outside, and always on window replacement.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in McKinley Park.

The community-area tables stop at 1970 and never draw a 1978 line. What they give is 77.9 percent built before 1970, which is a floor rather than an answer, and no source puts a number on the gap for McKinley Park. That puts most of the housing inside the federal lead-safe renovation rule, which attaches to pre-1978 homes and to work that disturbs the paint on them. In Illinois it is administered by EPA rather than by a state agency.

In McKinley Park it is worth asking about before the work starts rather than after the sanding has. Ask whoever you hire to say, in plain terms, how they intend to handle it at your particular address.

McKinley Park runs to a median build year of 1930 across 6,249 housing units, 77.9 percent of which predate 1970. Prewar stock alone is 62.8 percent. Nothing about that mix is a fast repaint.

McKinley Park is 70.2 percent owner occupied, 3,989 households against 1,697 renting. 56.3 percent of units are in buildings of two or more, 6.2 percent are attached, and the remaining 37.3 percent are detached houses averaging 5.9 rooms. The Census puts the median home value at $303,496.

McKinley Park is in the top four of the 22 Chicago community areas covered here for the largest prewar share (62.8 percent, first of them all), the oldest housing by median build year (1930, first of them all) and the smallest housing stock overall (6,249 units). It is also near the top for the smallest owner-occupied market (3,989 households).

Where McKinley Park departs most from the 76 place average: prewar housing at 62.8 percent against a 15.8 percent average, housing in buildings of two or more at 56.3 percent against a 29 percent average and detached houses at 37.3 percent against a 61.8 percent average.

Source: Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning, Community Data Snapshots 2026, drawing on American Community Survey 2024 estimates. Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.
